item.title: Microclimate persistence in island montane cloud forests
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04168-6

Montane cloud forests maintain stable near-surface humidity despite regional warming, buffered by water-vapor supply, cloud-mediated cooling, and thermodynamic regulation, based on a 42-year high-resolution analysis of hourly climate data from Taiwan.
item.dc:title: Microclimate persistence in island montane cloud forests

item.title: Self-supervised temporal reconstruction of reanalysis fields at subhourly scales
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04211-6

This article proposes a token-guided self-supervised framework that reconstructs 15-minute near-surface relative humidity and air temperature from coarse reanalysis records without high-frequency training data, providing support for fast-evolving weather events.
item.dc:title: Self-supervised temporal reconstruction of reanalysis fields at subhourly scales

item.title: Accelerating anthropogenic influence on annual peak wood density and associated carbon accumulation across northern conifers
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04198-0

Reconstructions based on tree-ring and hourly temperature data identify an optimal thermal range across northern conifers and link rising optimal-temperature hours to anthropogenic warming and biomass and carbon gains, with further increases projected
item.dc:title: Accelerating anthropogenic influence on annual peak wood density and associated carbon accumulation across northern conifers

item.title: Household affordability of sanitary landfilling is governed by cost allocation rather than metropolitan economic capacity
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04208-1

Across six megacities, sanitary landfills are technically feasible, with suitable landfill land and tipping fees ranging from 54–129 US dollars per tonne, but household affordability is a challenge, according to a spatial landfill siting, engineering-cost modeling, and satellite-derived GDP.
item.dc:title: Household affordability of sanitary landfilling is governed by cost allocation rather than metropolitan economic capacity
item.dc:creator: Yugo Sato
Guanghao Chen

item.title: Energetically extreme fires drive disastrous societal impacts
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04217-0

Disastrous wildfires are disproportionately associated with exceptionally high fire energy, according to a global analysis linking 20.76 million fires from 2002–2025 with disaster records and exposure datasets.
item.dc:title: Energetically extreme fires drive disastrous societal impacts

item.title: Sedimentary controls on pyrite sulfur isotopes in euxinic settings
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04178-4

Pyrite sulfur isotopes record substantial sedimentary overprinting, reflecting progressive modification of sedimentary pyrite during burial and a sedimentary origin for much of the water-column sulfide, according to microscale and bulk sulfur isotope measurements of pyrite from the Black Sea water column and sediments.
item.dc:title: Sedimentary controls on pyrite sulfur isotopes in euxinic settings

item.title: Transitional calcite-aragonite stacking as a signature of hexagonal aragonite in biogenic and inorganic deposits
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04166-8

The presence of (001) stacking faults and (0001) calcite twins testifies to the formation of transitional calcite-aragonite structures, suggesting the occurrence of a hexarag precursor phase relevant to metastable aragonite formation, as shown using electron microscopy and structural modeling combined with theory-based optimization.
item.dc:title: Transitional calcite-aragonite stacking as a signature of hexagonal aragonite in biogenic and inorganic deposits

item.title: Environmental flexibility across dynamic Cambrian ecosystems fueled trilobite success
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04205-4

Trilobites, traditionally viewed as strictly marine animals, are identified within river- and wave-influenced delta deposits, characterized by variable salinity and episodic freshwater influence, according to multiproxy geochemical analyses of Cambrian strata in Morocco.
item.dc:title: Environmental flexibility across dynamic Cambrian ecosystems fueled trilobite success

item.title: Radiation regimes shape microbial light-harvesting strategies and network organization on glacier surfaces
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04196-2

Arctic and Tibetan glacier cryoconite microbial communities differ in energy strategies, network organization, and metabolic potential, with rhodopsin-based phototrophy favored in the Arctic and photosynthesis in Tibet, as shown by comparative metagenomic analyses.

item.title: Algal-bacterial synergy in marimo granules enables low-carbon advanced nitrogen removal from wastewater
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04215-2

Elevated nitrate reprograms marimo nitrogen cycling by water type, boosting nitrate removal and enriching a core consortium led by Rhodobacteraceae for stable performance, according to metagenomic and correlation analyses.

item.title: Polar front jet regulates tropical sea surface temperature impacts on South China extreme precipitation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04194-4

Record precipitation over South China in April–May 2024 resulted from low-level moisture convergence associated with a trough between two anomalous anticyclones, according to statistical diagnostics and model simulations.
item.dc:title: Polar front jet regulates tropical sea surface temperature impacts on South China extreme precipitation

item.title: Distinct intraseasonal pathways driving rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China and their subseasonal predictability
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04031-8

Rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China are classified into four types with distinct intraseasonal physical pathways, with tropical-driven events showing the highest predictability and dual-extratropical-wave-train events the lowest, as revealed by observations and climate model experiments.
item.dc:title: Distinct intraseasonal pathways driving rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China and their subseasonal predictability

item.title: Widespread tree-cover gains across Europe over two decades were strongest in regions of agricultural retreat
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04190-8

Across Europe, tree-cover gains from 2001 to 2021 generally increased connectivity while reducing tree-cover heterogeneity, particularly in landscapes with more former cropland, according to an integrated framework quantifying tree cover, connectivity and tree-cover heterogeneity.
item.dc:title: Widespread tree-cover gains across Europe over two decades were strongest in regions of agricultural retreat

item.title: Erosion carbon dynamics extend beyond carbon accounting to ecological significance
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04203-6

Erosion is not only a process affecting land–atmosphere carbon exchange, but also a process that reorganizes the spatial and functional ecological states in which carbon is retained, transformed, or buried across landscapes, based on a framework viewing erosion as soil functional-layer reorganization.
item.dc:title: Erosion carbon dynamics extend beyond carbon accounting to ecological significance
item.dc:creator: Liangang Xiao

item.title: Large intraplate earthquakes on an extinct oceanic plate reveal fracture zone reactivation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04197-1

Cessation of plate-boundary activity at oceanic fracture zones does not imply mechanical quiescence, these can be reactivated under present-day stress conditions, shown through analysis of two earthquakes that occurred in 2025 within the former Phoenix Plate in the Drake Passage region.
item.dc:title: Large intraplate earthquakes on an extinct oceanic plate reveal fracture zone reactivation

item.title: Diversified cropping rotation increases soil carbon sequestration via fungal-mediated necromass production and mineral association
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04177-5

Crop diversification increased soil organic carbon by 10–15%, boosted microbial growth and carbon-use efficiency, shifted communities toward fungi, and raised mineral-associated carbon by 48–69%, based on a 43-year field trial and community transplantation assays.
item.dc:title: Diversified cropping rotation increases soil carbon sequestration via fungal-mediated necromass production and mineral association

item.title: Persistent influx of atmospheric microplastics and nanoplastics to Mount Everest driven by large scale circulation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04206-3

Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station exceed those at Everest Base Camp, reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences, with an estimated annual atmospheric input of 56 tons to the Tibetan Plateau above 4000 m, based on year-long monitoring on Mount Everest’s northern slope.

item.title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04188-2

Wildfire risk in the western United States increases during winter and spring in response to global warming, while summer fire weather extremes follow the variation of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, as revealed by analysis based on long-term reanalysis.
item.dc:title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US

item.title: Global warming intensifies compound renewable energy droughts
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04183-7

Global warming intensifies renewable energy droughts by reducing wind and solar resources, with greater warming leading to more severe renewable energy droughts, as indicated by climate model projections and machine learning analysis.
item.dc:title: Global warming intensifies compound renewable energy droughts
